date_semantics: checked_on records when a maintainer last opened and verified the linked Apple page; it is not the page publication or update date.

fixture_coverage_semantics.baseline: The family is emitted by audit_app for an empty project with empty metadata.
fixture_coverage_semantics.conditional: The family is not baseline and is emitted by the repository's synthetic conditional-coverage fixture.
fixture_coverage_semantics.regression: The family has a dedicated anonymized before/after regression fixture derived from an observed maintenance issue.
fixture_coverage_semantics.not-exercised: No baseline, synthetic conditional, or dedicated regression fixture covers the family.

Offering account deletion in your app
Managing your app's information property list values
Preserving your app's model data across launches

rules.trigger: The lowercased App Store description contains one of five exact fake or prank phrases such as 'fake gps' or 'prank charger'.
rules.limits: This is a narrow English substring heuristic with no context analysis; variants can be missed and legitimate explanations can be flagged.
rules.remediation: Review the full claim in context and remove, qualify, or substantiate wording that could misrepresent the app's behavior.

rules.trigger: The lowercased App Store description contains one of the detector's exact health-measurement or diagnosis phrases.
rules.limits: The phrase list is English-only and context-blind; it neither evaluates measurement accuracy nor proves a medical claim is unsafe.
rules.remediation: Manually verify the claimed method, supported hardware, accuracy evidence, disclaimers, and any applicable regulatory context.

rules.trigger: The category contains 'kids' or the description contains 'for kids', and a Swift source scan finds AdMob, FBAds, or GADBanner.
rules.limits: The signal uses a small case-sensitive SDK marker list and does not inspect ad configuration, data practices, or Apple's contextual-ad exceptions.
rules.remediation: Inspect the advertising integration and Kids Category exception criteria, then remove the SDK or document and configure an eligible contextual flow.

rules.trigger: The supportUrl field is present in fetched App Store Connect data but is empty; an absent field is reported as skipped.
rules.limits: This validates only presence of the fetched field and does not test URL reachability, page content, or every localization.
rules.remediation: Set the required localizable Support URL in App Store Connect and verify its public support page separately.

rules.trigger: The description field is present in fetched App Store Connect data but is empty or whitespace; an absent field is reported as skipped.
rules.limits: This checks field presence only and does not determine whether the description accurately represents a complete app.
rules.remediation: Provide the required App Store description, then review its claims and completeness with the separate advisory checks.

rules.trigger: A present, nonempty App Store description is 50 characters or shorter.
rules.limits: The 50-character threshold is a local heuristic rather than an Apple minimum, and an absent or empty description passes here because the official presence check handles it.
rules.remediation: Review whether the description clearly explains the core experience and add useful detail when the short copy omits important behavior.

rules.trigger: The lowercased description contains a whole-word match for lorem, todo, placeholder, tbd, or coming soon.
rules.limits: The fixed English regex can miss other unfinished copy and can flag intentional discussion of one of those terms.
rules.remediation: Inspect the matched text and replace unfinished copy or rephrase legitimate usage so the submitted metadata describes shipping behavior.

rules.trigger: The description mentions play along, playback, or tap to play, while Swift sources lack AVAudioEngine, AVAudioPlayer, and AudioServicesPlay markers.
rules.limits: This is a metadata-to-source heuristic over a few literal phrases and APIs; wrappers, other audio frameworks, and non-audio uses can change the result.
rules.remediation: Trace the promised playback flow in the built app and either implement it, point the source scan at its real marker, or correct the metadata.

rules.trigger: The description contains 'identify' plus either the substring 'ai' or 'photo', while Swift sources lack VNCoreMLRequest, MLModel, and URLSession markers.
rules.limits: Broad substrings and a small implementation-marker set make this a noisy signal; local wrappers, other inference stacks, or unrelated text can be misclassified.
rules.remediation: Exercise the identification feature and either align its implementation with the claim or revise metadata that overstates the shipped capability.

rules.trigger: The notes key is present and its lowercased value is 200 characters or shorter.
rules.limits: Apple publishes no 200-character minimum; length alone cannot measure whether concise notes explain every non-obvious review path.
rules.remediation: Review the notes for actionable setup, access, and test context, expanding them only where reviewers would otherwise lack needed information.

rules.trigger: The notes key is present and keyword groups cover fewer than three of four topics: purpose, test steps, external services, and regional behavior.
rules.limits: Simple English keyword groups approximate useful coverage; they can miss equivalent wording, localized notes, or a topic that does not apply.
rules.remediation: Manually add relevant purpose, test-path, dependency, and region details while omitting topics that genuinely do not apply.

rules.trigger: The fetched App Store name exceeds 30 Python string characters.
rules.limits: The check applies Python length to the fetched value; a missing name becomes an empty string and passes, and display rendering is not evaluated.
rules.remediation: Shorten the App Store name to the published 30-character maximum and verify the final localized display in App Store Connect.

rules.trigger: A parsed CFBundleDisplayName differs from both the full App Store name and its prefix before the first title separator.
rules.limits: Only the first discovered Info.plist and simple XML string entries are parsed; build settings, localized display names, and acceptable branding variations can be missed.
rules.remediation: Compare the built app label with App Store metadata and align the names or document an intentional, reviewer-clear brand variation.

rules.trigger: The lowercased description contains the whole word android or the phrase google play.
rules.limits: This text heuristic does not interpret context or Apple's approved-interactive-functionality exception and misses other platform references.
rules.remediation: Inspect the reference in context, remove irrelevant cross-platform marketing, or confirm that the cited exception fits the submitted experience.

rules.trigger: A supported NSUsageDescription key is parsed from Info.plist, but Swift sources lack the common framework or API markers mapped to that key.
rules.limits: The family covers eleven keys using regexes over Swift files; wrappers, dependencies, generated plists, and indirect use can produce false signals.
rules.remediation: Confirm the protected-resource flow, then remove an unused declaration or align the implementation and purpose text with the actual access.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall plus referenced localization text mentions a trial, but the combined text lacks either a post-trial timing marker or a price or renewal marker.
rules.limits: The scan recognizes a small English and Chinese vocabulary across source text, not the rendered offer, StoreKit product data, or every locale.
rules.remediation: Review the rendered trial offer and clearly present what happens after the trial, including applicable timing, price, and renewal information.

rules.trigger: A PaywallView.swift or SubscriptionView.swift is found, but its source plus localization text lacks the detector's common English or Chinese renewal wording.
rules.limits: This heuristic neither renders the paywall nor covers every valid phrase; Apple does not prescribe the literal words 'auto-renewing'.
rules.remediation: Manually confirm that the visible offer clearly communicates price, duration, and renewal behavior in each supported locale.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall source lacks one of the detector's specific 30-point-or-larger bold system-font patterns or bold title and largeTitle patterns.
rules.limits: Typography regexes do not measure the rendered hierarchy, custom fonts, dynamic type, contrast, or localization; Apple publishes no 36-point rule.
rules.remediation: Inspect the rendered paywall across devices and locales, then make the price and billing cadence visually clear using the project's actual design system.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall source contains no case-insensitive 'restore' text marker.
rules.limits: A label match does not prove that restoration works, while localized labels or a restore flow outside the selected paywall file can be missed.
rules.remediation: Exercise an accessible restore flow for restorable purchases and expose it clearly on or from the purchase experience.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall source does not contain the case-sensitive substring 'rivacy'.
rules.limits: The substring is only a source marker; it can miss localized or indirect links and does not prove that a matching label opens a reachable policy.
rules.remediation: Verify that the rendered paywall offers a clear, working Privacy Policy link in the supported purchase locales.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall source contains none of the detector's Terms, EULA, or stdeula text markers.
rules.limits: A source-text match does not prove a visible, tappable, or reachable legal link, and localized or indirect implementations can be missed.
rules.remediation: Verify that the rendered paywall exposes a clear, working Terms of Use or EULA link in each supported purchase locale.

rules.trigger: Subscription signals exist, but the lowercased App Store description contains none of the configured EULA, terms, agreement, or terms-URL markers.
rules.limits: This heuristic inspects description text only; it does not read App Store agreement fields, custom license metadata, linked page content, or every language.
rules.remediation: Review the applicable subscription metadata and agreement setup, then add an accurate Terms or EULA reference where users and reviewers can find it.

rules.trigger: A Swift file matches one of three regexes resembling feature access gated on an App Store rating.
rules.limits: The regexes are narrow, generally single-line, and context-blind; they neither cover every coercive flow nor prove a match executes as gating.
rules.remediation: Trace each match through the user flow and remove rating-dependent access or refactor misleading code that is not actually coercive.

rules.trigger: The project has fewer than two detected custom views, a combined view-service-model score below three, and fewer than four non-boilerplate Swift files.
rules.limits: Filename and declaration counts are only a project-shape signal; small apps can be substantial, while many files do not establish useful functionality.
rules.remediation: Evaluate the shipping experience manually and strengthen genuine user-facing utility rather than adding files solely to satisfy the heuristic.

rules.trigger: The project has fewer than three detected custom views, a combined view-service-model score below four, and fewer than five non-boilerplate Swift files.
rules.limits: This is a coarse shape heuristic and does not compare binaries, templates, content, branding, or functionality with other App Store apps.
rules.remediation: Manually assess whether the product offers a distinct, durable experience and improve real differentiation where it is thin.

rules.trigger: Swift sources contain a GIDSignIn, FBSDKLogin, or TwitterAuth marker but no SignInWithAppleButton or ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider marker.
rules.limits: The fixed SDK marker list misses other providers and wrappers, and the source scan cannot determine whether a Guideline 4.8 exception applies.
rules.remediation: Review the actual authentication options and exceptions, then add an equivalent Sign in with Apple flow or document why the exception fits.

rules.trigger: Swift sources contain a UNUserNotificationCenter marker but no common authorization-request marker.
rules.limits: Source markers do not prove an actual opt-in UI or execution order; wrappers and alternate APIs can be missed.
rules.remediation: Manually exercise notification onboarding and confirm a user-initiated authorization flow before notifications are enabled.

rules.trigger: The privacyPolicyUrl field is present in fetched App Store Connect data but is empty; an absent field is reported as skipped.
rules.limits: This validates only presence of the fetched App Store Connect field and does not test reachability, policy contents, or in-app access.
rules.remediation: Set the Privacy Policy URL required for every app, then verify the public policy and in-app link separately.

source_refs.section: Describing how your app uses data

rules.trigger: Swift sources contain none of four common Privacy Policy text, symbol, URL-path, or Chinese-label patterns.
rules.limits: The static marker scan does not render navigation or validate tap behavior, and localized strings, web content, or abstractions can be missed.
rules.remediation: Exercise the app's privacy entry point and make the current policy easy to find and open from the relevant in-app surface.

rules.trigger: A nonempty Privacy Policy URL returns a non-2xx/3xx status or raises an error during an eight-second HTTPS-aware HEAD request.
rules.limits: HEAD requests can be rejected even when browser GET works, and the probe does not assess policy content, geography, authentication, or long-term availability.
rules.remediation: Open the exact public URL in a normal browser and fix genuine TLS, redirect, access, or hosting failures found during that check.

rules.trigger: A nonempty Support URL returns a non-2xx/3xx status or raises an error during an eight-second HEAD request.
rules.limits: Some hosts reject HEAD while serving browser GET successfully, and the probe does not evaluate whether the page provides useful support.
rules.remediation: Open the exact URL in a normal browser and correct genuine TLS, redirect, public-access, or support-page failures.

rules.trigger: Swift sources contain an account-like sign-in or registration marker but no common deleteAccount or account-delete marker.
rules.limits: Source names are only a signal; external account systems, wrappers, localized UI, and deletion flows with different identifiers can be missed.
rules.remediation: Walk the real account lifecycle and provide an accessible in-app deletion path where accounts are created, or clarify why no account exists.

rules.trigger: The fetched simulated-gambling answer is present and is not the placeholder '?'; the finding is emitted as an informational passing signal for manual comparison.
rules.limits: This rule never fails and cannot infer real-money gaming, legal eligibility, or whether the questionnaire answer matches gameplay.
rules.remediation: Compare the recorded simulated-gambling value with the shipping content and correct the age-rating questionnaire if they differ.

rules.trigger: The appStoreAgeRating field is present but is not one of the detector's published non-UNRATED enumeration values; an absent field is reported as skipped.
rules.limits: This validates the fetched enumeration only and does not verify that questionnaire answers accurately describe the app's content.
rules.remediation: Complete and save the required age-rating questionnaire until App Store Connect returns a valid published rating, then verify its answers manually.

rules.trigger: The fetched appinfo_state is exactly REJECTED; an absent state is reported as skipped and every other value passes.
rules.limits: This observes one AppInfo state and does not diagnose its cause or prove that the complete app version is submission-ready.
rules.remediation: Re-save the Age Rating in the App Store Connect web UI as indicated, then fetch AppInfo again and investigate if REJECTED persists.

rules.trigger: The lowercased description contains one of seven exact regulated-industry phrases covering banking, medical monitoring, crypto exchange, or gambling.
rules.limits: A keyword is only a review signal; this scan neither classifies the service nor checks licenses, legal entity, geography, or account eligibility.
rules.remediation: Identify the precise regulated activity and manually verify its licensing, entity, market, and review-note context before submission.

rules.trigger: The description contains 'share' plus either 'data' or 'personal', while Swift sources lack the detector's common consent and sharing-control markers.
rules.limits: Broad English substrings and source regexes can misread non-personal sharing or miss consent implemented through wrappers, web flows, or other names.
rules.remediation: Trace the real personal-data sharing path and expose clear user choice and controls, or revise metadata that inaccurately describes sharing.

rules.trigger: The lowercased description mentions famous quote, movie clip, song lyric, or celebrity; any such match emits a failing heuristic.
rules.limits: The detector does not inspect assets, provenance, licenses, public-domain status, or the context in which the phrase appears.
rules.remediation: Verify ownership or licensing for the referenced content and retain evidence, or remove claims and assets that cannot be supported.

rules.trigger: Parsed plist values contain NetworkExtension or the description contains 'vpn', while the lowercased review notes contain no 'vpn' marker.
rules.limits: The signal does not inspect entitlements, network behavior, organization status, or Guideline 5.4 eligibility, and its metadata markers are incomplete.
rules.remediation: Review the VPN or Network Extension implementation and account eligibility, then add concise setup and behavior context to review notes.

rules.trigger: The first 300 description characters contain a configured detector, scanner, or meter keyword, but the first 500 characters and review notes lack known hardware-context phrases.
rules.limits: The English keyword windows are heuristic and can miss equivalent disclosures, localized copy, or hardware context presented elsewhere.
rules.remediation: Clarify whether the feature uses built-in sensors, external hardware, HealthKit, or a software-only method in metadata or review notes.

rules.trigger: The description contains health, medical, or wellness but not menstr, and parsed plist string values contain no case-sensitive HealthKit marker; the result is emitted as a passing caution.
rules.limits: This rule never fails, does not inspect entitlements or source imports, and broad keywords can identify apps with no HealthKit use case.
rules.remediation: Review whether the health wording accurately describes the implementation and explain the data source or add an appropriate HealthKit integration where applicable.

rules.trigger: A nonempty fetched subscription state is outside APPROVED, WAITING_FOR_REVIEW, IN_REVIEW, and READY_TO_SUBMIT; accepted or absent states emit no finding.
rules.limits: The top-level sub_state reflects the first populated subscription returned by the fetch and does not establish readiness of every product or the app version.
rules.remediation: Resolve the observed product's App Store Connect state, then re-fetch the full subscription catalog before assembling the intended review submission.

rules.trigger: For each fetched subscription availability entry, a territory count of zero fails and any positive count passes.
rules.limits: The check counts returned territory records only; it does not validate pricing, storefront propagation, product state, or whether those territories match launch intent.
rules.remediation: Configure at least one intended available territory for the subscription, then query availability again and test the product in an eligible storefront.

rules.trigger: A fetched subscription has between one and forty-nine available territories; zero is handled by the readiness family and fifty or more emits no advisory.
rules.limits: The threshold is a launch-coverage heuristic, not a universal distribution target, and territory count alone says nothing about intended markets or pricing.
rules.remediation: Compare the configured territories with the product's launch plan and add or remove markets only to match that documented intent.

rules.trigger: Each fetched subscription whose state is exactly READY_TO_SUBMIT emits a failing readiness finding; other states emit no finding.
rules.limits: The detector treats READY_TO_SUBMIT as a first-submission signal but does not independently determine whether the item is the first product of its type.
rules.remediation: Confirm the product's submission history and, for the first subscription of its type, include it with a new app-version submission before rechecking state.

rules.trigger: Any fetched subscription-group localization state is outside APPROVED, WAITING_FOR_REVIEW, and IN_REVIEW; an empty list passes.
rules.limits: This snapshot heuristic does not query StoreKit visibility directly, distinguish every valid lifecycle transition, or prove the localization caused catalog unavailability.
rules.remediation: Inspect the listed group localizations in App Store Connect, resolve unfinished review states, and verify catalog visibility in the intended storefront.

rules.trigger: Swift sources contain Product.products or Transaction.currentEntitlements but no Transaction.updates marker anywhere in the scanned project.
rules.limits: A global source marker cannot prove listener lifecycle or entitlement freshness, and wrappers or another synchronization strategy can be missed.
rules.remediation: Trace asynchronous purchase, renewal, refund, and revocation updates and add or document a durable entitlement-refresh strategy.

rules.trigger: A non-excluded Swift file directly assigns true to .isPremium or .isSubscribed and lacks a same-file demo-mode marker.
rules.limits: Regex and path exclusions can miss aliases or flag legitimate test and migration code; it does not trace whether the write actually bypasses StoreKit.
rules.remediation: Trace each direct write and route production entitlement state through verified StoreKit transactions, isolating any demo or test override explicitly.

rules.trigger: A project with CKContainer(identifier:) has a recognized sync, push, upload, saveTo, or backup function that saves a constructed CKRecord without record(for:) in that body or a called fetch-prefixed helper.
rules.limits: The parser recognizes limited function signatures and names, treats any matching fetch in the body as sufficient regardless of order, and cannot infer record identity or save policy at runtime.
rules.remediation: Review each affected record lifecycle and fetch or otherwise reconcile the existing server record before saving updates with an intentional conflict policy.

rules.trigger: Swift source constants expose one or more rootRecordType or recordType string values while cloudkit_production_schema_verified is false or absent.
rules.limits: Static extraction covers only literal assignments, and the caller-supplied verification flag does not itself query or prove the deployed production schema.
rules.remediation: Export or inspect the production CloudKit schema for the listed record types and set the verification input only after confirming deployment.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall or its directly referenced L10n constants match one of twelve configured benefit claims, while project Swift sources lack that benefit's implementation markers.
rules.limits: Fixed claim and regex pairs are heuristic; icon arguments are stripped, but indirect copy, wrappers, alternate implementations, and source markers unrelated to the feature can still skew results.
rules.remediation: Exercise the named benefit end to end and either ship the claimed behavior, teach the detector its real implementation marker, or remove inaccurate paywall copy.

rules.trigger: The fetched locales_missing_support field is present and lists at least one localization; an absent field is reported as skipped.
rules.limits: This trusts the fetcher's missing-locale list and does not test each URL's reachability, page content, or the completeness of the locale inventory.
rules.remediation: Populate the required Support URL for every listed localization and re-fetch App Store Connect metadata to confirm the list is empty.

rules.trigger: One of seven custom NSUsageDescription keys is parsed from Info.plist, but Swift sources lack its broader mapped framework or API markers.
rules.limits: Regexes over Swift and a simple plist parser cannot see every wrapper, dependency, generated value, or indirect protected-resource use, so this is an unused-declaration signal only.
rules.remediation: Confirm the real protected-resource flow, then remove an unused declaration or align its implementation and user-facing purpose text.

rules.trigger: A discovered paywall contains a regex-recognized Privacy or Terms Link with a nearby faded white foreground style and no explicit blue override.
rules.limits: The source-window heuristic does not render color, contrast, inheritance, themes, accessibility settings, or custom styles and can miss differently structured links.
rules.remediation: Inspect both legal links in the rendered paywall and apply a clearly visible, tappable style with adequate contrast in every theme.

rules.trigger: A regex-recognized @Model class declares a Bool, Int, Double, String, or Date property on a bare line without an inline default.
rules.limits: The parser ignores many Swift types and layouts and cannot determine initializer behavior, store history, schema versioning, or whether a migration is compatible.
rules.remediation: Review each field against existing stores and provide a compatible default, initializer, or explicit migration plan as appropriate.

rules.trigger: A Swift file contains a configured direct AI endpoint, URLSession or request.httpBody, and a quoted messages key, but no quoted model key.
rules.limits: This text heuristic can miss constructed payloads and can flag proxies that legitimately inject a default model; it does not send or validate the request.
rules.remediation: Trace the selected provider or proxy contract and add an explicit model field when the endpoint expects one, otherwise document the injected default.

rules.trigger: A Swift file uses one of seven empty-prone API families and assigns error.localizedDescription to errorMessage inside a generic catch, while the file lacks that family's configured empty or not-found markers.
rules.limits: Regexes do not model control flow: an unrelated marker anywhere in the file can suppress a signal, and typed handling through helpers or different UI state names can be missed.
rules.remediation: Exercise no-data, not-found, denied, offline, and genuine-failure paths; map expected empty conditions to friendly empty states and preserve actionable errors separately.

rules.trigger: A recognized release-notes file, or the newest parsed CHANGELOG section, contains more than 4,000 Python string characters.
rules.limits: Only configured local paths are scanned; the check does not fetch App Store Connect text, normalize final pasted content, or assess note quality, and emoji are not rejected.
rules.remediation: Trim each affected What's New source to the published 4,000-character limit while preserving concise user-facing release value.
